question_text: Classify each variable as categorical, discrete, or continuous:

subparts.stem: The number of houses on a particular street.
subparts.solution: The number of houses on a particular street can be counted, so it is a discrete variable.

ai_explanation.concept_rule: A discrete variable takes on distinct, separate countable values (usually integers).
step_by_step: Identify that houses can only be counted in whole numbers.
Conclude the data is discrete numerical.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Classifying discrete numerical data as continuous.

subparts.stem: The number of hours spent travelling on an airplane.
subparts.solution: The number of hours spent travelling on an airplane can be measured and can take any value between certain limits, so it is a continuous variable.

ai_explanation.concept_rule: A continuous variable can take any real value within a given interval and is measured rather than counted.
step_by_step: Determine whether time is measured or counted: it is measured.
Recognize that time can take fractional/decimal values, making it continuous.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Thinking time is discrete because it is rounded to whole hours.

subparts.stem: The brand of laptop someone uses.
subparts.solution: The brand of laptop someone uses is a categorical variable.

ai_explanation.concept_rule: Categorical variables describe qualities or characteristics and consist of labels or names.
step_by_step: Identify that laptop brands are names (e.g., Apple, Dell, Lenovo).
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Confusing categorical data with discrete numerical data.
